newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.N. concerned over threat to Afghan Buddhas.
newsitem.headline: U.N. concerned over threat to Afghan Buddhas.

text.p: The United Nations expressed concern to Afghanistan's dominant Taleban Islamic movement on Wednesday over a Taleban threat to destroy giant statues of Buddha, a U.N. source said.
The source, based in Pakistan, said Taleban responded that no decision had yet been yet been taken on the fate of the statues in the central Afghan province of Bamiyan.

A Taleban commander in the area said last week his purist Islamic militia would destroy the statues on religious grounds after capturing Bamiyan from the opposition Shi'ite Moslem faction of Hezb-i-Wahdat.
"We will destroy them because Islam has forbidden statues," commander Ahmadzai told reporters.
The source said U.N. official Francis Okelo raised the issue with Mullah Hassan, Taleban governor of the southern Afghan town of Kandahar.

Okelo said no action should be taken against the statues and reminded Hassan of a U.N. General Assembly resolution that called last year for the preservation of monuments and culture in war-shattered Afghanistan.
Hassan told Okelo that "no decision has been taken so far and that it is for the Ulema (Islamic scholars) to decide about the matter", the source said.

The Taleban, seeking to advance to Bamiyan, have been held at bay by Hezb-i-Wahdat, which is defending the strategic Shibar Pass that controls access to Bamiyan city and opens a route to the opposition-controlled north.
Okelo has been meeting Afghan faction leaders in a bid to restart U.N.-mediated peace talks between them.
